title: Tulpamancy: Guide Into the Strange and Wonderful
author: Luigi.exe (also u/Eeveecraft), with contributions credited to 'Darkflame'
edition_cited: Google Doc re-archived as PDF in archive.org item 'tulpamancy'; OCR text used
locator_hints: Section Fourteen: Visualization (methods one to four)
Section Fifteen: Imposition: spatial awareness, then 'Method One: Wall Method', 'Method Two: Darkness Method', 'Method Three (EXPERIMENTAL): Sensory Control Method' (printed pages 23-25)
summary: A long community guide whose Section Fifteen treats visual imposition as a controlled, intentional hallucination seen in the physical world without using the mind's eye. It gives three methods. Wall method: sit upright before a plain white wall in dimmed light, impose the figure flat on the wall for at least a few minutes without looking away, over many sessions, until a faint outline, shadow or distortion is seen. Darkness method: in a fully blacked-out room with eyes wide open, impose the figure, or first a simple glowing sphere of light, blink sparingly and let it 'burn in' until it is seen even with closed eyes, then reintroduce room light gradually. A third, experimental method is flagged as untested. It warns that visual imposition is rare, tedious, and can become hard to switch off.
why_relevant: Explicit step-by-step community instruction for making a deliberately imagined object (including a glowing sphere) become seen with open eyes, starting from someone who sees nothing; states expected first signs and failure modes.

date_evidence.basis: archive.org stamps the item 'tulpamancy' with addeddate/publicdate 2020-04-14; the uploader says the files were Google Docs downloaded and re-archived. The document prints no date of its own (searched for year strings and 'last edit'); it links a Reddit comment in r/Tulpas whose date I could not see. So the date is a latest-possible date, not a writing date.

author_basis: Pseudonymous: signs as Luigi.exe on Discord, Eeveecraft on Steam, u/Eeveecraft on Reddit. No real name.
notes: OCR text of a PDF; page numbers appear as bare numerals between paragraphs. The guide carries a strong mental-health warning at the top. Other sections (vocality, possession, switching) are out of scope.
